 Position Summary The Pereira Laboratory in the Department of Radiology at WashU Medicine is seeking a highly motivated Postdoctoral Research Associate to join a multidisciplinary, NIH-funded research program at the interface of molecular imaging, antibody engineering, cancer biology, drug development, and translational oncology. Our laboratory develops next-generation antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs), molecular imaging agents, and targeted therapeutics to improve cancer diagnosis and treatment. We combine protein engineering, chemical biology, molecular imaging, computational biology, and spatial transcriptomics to understand therapeutic response and accelerate translation from preclinical discovery to clinical application. The successful candidate will have experimental and analytical skills, excellent scientific writing and communication abilities, and the capacity to work both independently and collaboratively. Candidates should be highly motivated, organized, and eager to integrate experimental and computational approaches to address translational research questions while mentoring junior trainees and contributing to a positive laboratory environment. Candidates should have demonstrated research experience in one or more of the following areas: antibody engineering, antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs), cancer biology, molecular imaging, or chemical biology. Experience with computational analysis of spatial transcriptomics or other high-dimensional datasets and strong data management skills are highly desirable. We are seeking an independent and collaborative scientist interested in developing innovative antibody-based therapeutics while integrating computational approaches to study tumor biology and mechanisms of response and resistance. Job Description Primary Duties & Responsibilities: Information on being a postdoc at WashU in St. Louis can be found at https://postdoc.wustl.edu/prospective-postdocs-2/ . Trains under the supervision of a faculty mentor including (but not limited to): Design and execute independent research projects focused on antibody engineering, ADC development, molecular imaging, and theragnostic agents. Develop and evaluate novel antibody conjugates using molecular, cellular, biochemical, and in vivo approaches. Perform cancer biology studies using cell lines, patient-derived models, and mouse models. Analyze and integrate molecular imaging, spatial transcriptomics, and other multi-omics datasets to identify biomarkers and mechanisms of therapeutic response. Develop computational workflows for spatial biology and imaging data analysis using R, Python, or related tools. Design experiments, analyze data, troubleshoot technical challenges, and critically interpret scientific findings. Organize, manage, and integrate experimental datasets in compliance with laboratory, institutional, and NIH data management and reproducibility standards. Prepare manuscripts, fellowship applications, grant proposals, and present research at national and international scientific meetings. Mentor graduate students and other laboratory trainees while contributing to a collaborative research environment. The individual must be physically able to wear protective equipment and to provide standard care to research animals. Salary Range: Base pay is commensurate with experience. job_67cd35d30e01bd90: Professor and Chair, Department of Emergency Medicine Position Overview School / Campus / College: School of Medicine Organization: Chairs - School of Medicine Title: Professor and Chair, Department of Emergency Medicine Position Details Position Description The University of Washington (UW) School of Medicine (SOM) is recruiting a Chair of the Department of Emergency Medicine. The Department operates three emergency departments in Seattle: including the UW Medical Center Montlake and Northwest campuses, and one at Harborview Medical Center, the only level I adult and pediatric trauma and burn center for a four-state region. These emergency departments combined treat over 130,000 patients per year, providing care for their communities and the region. This vision includes the opportunity to design a new, state-of-the-art emergency department at Harborview Medical Center, implementing workflows and technology to improve patient outcomes, integrating emergency services with the continuum of hospital and ambulatory care, and building collaborations to provide the highest quality of care. The chair will be a strong supporter of research, providing guidance and expertise to investigators at all different career stages. The chair will also be focused on workforce development, including supporting the Department’s educational programs, recruiting faculty, and providing mentorship to develop faculty as clinicians, educators, researchers, and leaders. With the rapid pace of transformation in academic medicine and emergency medicine, the chair will support a culture that emphasizes well-being during a period of change. The chair will be a visionary leader with a strong commitment to advancing education, research, clinical care, health equity, and well-being. The Department works closely with Airlift Northwest, which transports more than 4,500 patients every year across Washington, Wyoming, Alaska, Montana, Idaho, and Oregon. The appointment is expected to begin in Fall 2026, or as soon as practicable thereafter. The Andlinger Center is focused on resolving critical challenges to assuring a secure, resilient, and sustainable energy and environmental future. The post-doctoral researcher will report to Chris Greig and collaborate with researchers across engineering, computer science, and operations research. The successful candidate will contribute to an applied research project examining whether blockchain-enabled tokenization of low-carbon attributes can support credible and scalable virtual chain-of-custody systems—and thereby improve the bankability of industrial decarbonization projects. The research will develop and evaluate a system architecture that combines distributed-ledger technology with measurement, reporting and verification, mass-balance accounting, and third-party certification. The initial use case will examine low-carbon ethylene and polyethylene value chains, in which physical materials may be commingled while verified environmental attributes are transferred digitally from producers to downstream manufacturers and brand owners. The researcher will compare conventional undifferentiated commodity sales, bilateral green-premium contracts, and token-based aggregation of dispersed downstream willingness to pay. Analysis will consider the implications for revenue visibility, risk allocation, financing costs, debt capacity, and final investment decisions for capital-intensive projects, including a large-scale steam-cracker retrofit. Job Posting Title Assistant Professor of Biological Sciences Job Description Summary Faculty Job Description The Biological Sciences Department at Wellesley College invites applications for a tenure-track position in vertebrate biology at the rank of Assistant Professor to begin in Fall 2027. We seek to hire a broadly trained vertebrate biologist who is strongly committed to excellence in both teaching and research in an undergraduate liberal arts college environment. The position is open to candidates whose research is at the organismal level and addresses questions of physiology or form and function. A Ph.D. is required at the time of application. Candidates are expected to develop an active and productive research program that involves Wellesley undergraduates. A competitive start-up package will be provided. Candidates will be expected to teach the equivalent of four courses per year within the Biological Sciences curriculum. This will include introductory organismal biology and a course in comparative anatomy and physiology of vertebrates. In addition, the successful candidate will develop and offer an advanced course in their specialty. We welcome candidates with familiarity and/or experience with best practices in inclusive STEM pedagogies to apply. Applications are due Friday, September 11, 2026 and should be submitted via our application web site ( https://www.wellesley.edu/about-us/working-at-wellesley ). Materials must include 1) a cover letter (ca. 1-2 pages), 2) curriculum vitae, 3) a statement of teaching philosophy, experience, and interests, and how those inform your pedagogical practices (ca. 2-3 pages), 4) a statement of research accomplishments and plans for the future including the incorporation of undergraduates (ca. 2-4 pages), and 5) the names/email addresses of three references who will be asked to submit confidential letters of recommendation. Individually, the three letters of recommendation can be from any prior or current component of the candidate’s education or experience, but collectively, they should explicitly speak to the candidate’s promise for both successful teaching and research. First-round interviews will be held on Zoom in early to mid-October with campus visits in late October and November. Questions should be directed to the Biological Sciences search co-chairs, John Goss ( jgoss@wellesley.edu ) and Steven Biller ( sbiller@wellesley.edu ). The minimum salary for Assistant Professors is $103,000.00 annually.
